done_when: A follow-up that names a period the app reads itself (anything the app's date reader parses, such as last 30 days, explicit dates and date ranges, plus a month with or without a year, a year, a quarter with or without a year, or last, previous or this month, quarter or year) answers for that period whatever window the model emits; fiscal and other wording (FY, YTD, next month, previous week) keeps the model's window and the period control; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before, and an amount is never read as a year; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

findings.body: Fiscal wording is checked only after `parseTimeWindow` returns null. For `Show FY Q1 2025`, the existing parser at `backend/src/chat/timeWindowParse.ts:80` recognizes `Q1 2025` and returns calendar January–March, so the `FISCAL_PERIOD_PATTERN` branch is never evaluated and line 393 replaces the model's fiscal window. The same ordering affects inputs such as `YTD since 1 January`. These questions therefore lose the model's window and period control, contrary to the required fiscal exception.
findings.title: Not done: fiscal wording can still be overridden by the calendar parser

findings.body: The new period matrix still invokes `ChatService.ask` through `makeFixture` (`backend/src/chat/chat.service.test.ts:1319`), where the selector, executor/warehouse, audit, dimensions, reports, and resolver are fakes. The rerun test uses the same boundary, while frontend tests mock the API. The registered suite runs Node tests and Vitest (`package.json:26`; `frontend/package.json:9`) and has no Playwright/browser flow through a running API and real database. Thus named-period precedence, inheritance, amount protection, and edited-period reruns remain proven only at mocked service/jsdom boundaries. The successful close run executed those same commands, so this prior blocker remains open.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
